thread:
Priya: Quick sync after today's call with FinanceCo — they want a short POC. Need clear success criteria: latency, cost burn target, and an eval prompt set. They asked if we can guarantee a fallback to a smaller model when Dedicated capacity spikes.
Samir: Thanks — a couple quick answers: we can do canary + automatic fallback to a cheaper variant (same topology, quantized) at the routing layer. Fallback latency will be ~2x relative to the primary depending on model size.
Riley: For success criteria I recommend: (1) 95th pctile token latency <= 220ms for interactive flows, (2) avg cost <= $0.30 per 1k generated tokens post-batching, (3) end-to-end content accuracy pass rate >= 92% on their eval set.
Priya: Can you put that into a one-pager I can share? They want limits by route (chat vs batch) and a burn cap for the trial.
Riley: I'll draft. Also suggest we define prompt/eval families: Summarization, Slot-filling, and Safety checks. Example quick prompt for summarization eval: ```
Input: "Long earnings call transcript..."
Instruction: "Summarize key action items with company, owner, due date"
Expected: structured JSON with keys: actions, owners, deadlines
```
Jenna: Security note — they require KMS + SOC2 checklist. For Dedicated we can provide VPC peering + customer KMS. I'll attach the minimal answers for the questionnaire after this thread.
Priya: Burn cap — they asked for an initial 2-week trial with a hard spend cap. Wanted an estimate for 100k chat messages (avg 120 tokens in, 240 tokens out).
Samir: Rough math: 100k * 360 tokens = 36M tokens. If we assume $0.30 / 1k tokens => ~$10.8k. With batching and prefix caching we should drop to ~ $7–9k. Recommend offering a $9k trial cap.
Priya: Good. Also asked about rollback/quality gates — how do we define acceptance?
Riley: Acceptance gated on three checks: 
1) Latency SLO: 95th pctile across sample windows <= target (interactive 220ms / batch 2s).
2) Quality: Eval suite pass rate >= 92% for core prompts; no single prompt family < 85%.
3) Error budget: system errors < 0.5% and fallback usage < 15% over the trial window.
Priya: If they fail any gate, do we offer an extended trial or remediation?
Samir: Standard: propose a two-week remediation window where we work with SEs to tune batching/quantization and prompt templates. If still failing, we can offer an extended trial with an adjusted cap and a joint runbook.
Jenna: FYI on questionnaires — note on key management: customer-managed keys for S3 + model artifacts is supported for Dedicated. We'll need an MOU to capture responsibilities.
Priya: Ok next actions: Samir — confirm fallback model options and expected latency multiplier. Riley — prepare the eval prompt pack + pass thresholds. Jenna — prepare the minimal KMS + SOC2 answers. I'll compile a one-page POC scope and send to the customer.
ops-bot: Deploy checklist created: https://redwood.internal/ops/checklists/poc-1728654321 — owners: @Samir, @Riley, @Jenna. 
Priya: Thanks all! I'll update once customer signs the SOW. :thumbsup:
